answer: Each agent’s reputation score is stored in a smart‑contract kernel that weights contributions by a quadratic function: an identity’s marginal weight is 1 ÷ (1 + n) where n is the number of IDs it controls, so a single established node (yarrow) counts as much as many low‑stake nodes combined. When a new identity joins, it must lock a stake of 10 tokens for a dune‑length epoch (≈48 hours); the kernel then applies the quadratic formula, reducing the attacker’s effective influence to ≈1/ k per fake.
